articles.title: The Most Energetic Neutrino Ever Detected May Have Originated from a Blazar's Cosmic Cannon
articles.summary: In 2023, an underwater detector caught a neutrino with a staggering 220 PeV of energy—over ten times more powerful than any seen before. A new study suggests it came from blazars, supermassive black holes that shoot jets of plasma directly at Earth. The finding could unlock secrets of the universe's most extreme accelerators.

articles.title: A 380-Million-Year-Old Fish Skull Reveals Brain Adaptations for the Water-to-Land Transition
articles.summary: Using neutron imaging, researchers peered inside the skull of Koharalepis jarviki, a predatory fish from the Devonian. They found a brain similar to early tetrapods and adaptations for surface breathing, including openings on top of the skull. The fossil, the only one of its family with internal bones preserved, sheds light on how vertebrates conquered land.

articles.title: First-Ever Video of a Sperm Whale Birth Reveals Remarkable Cooperative Behavior Across Kin Groups
articles.summary: Scientists from Project CETI filmed a sperm whale giving birth off Dominica, capturing 34 minutes of unprecedented footage. A group of 10 whales, including non-relatives, assisted the mother, taking turns lifting the calf to breathe. The video and accompanying audio reveal complex social cooperation and vocal communication during this critical event.
